reviews.author: YennaPPa (Luscious.K)
reviews.text:
#Samseong-dong #Hyundai Department Store #Song

“Now it’s a precious home.”

In the past, there were a lot of buckwheat noodle restaurants.
There were mostly snack bars in front of the bus stop, and they made and sold dumplings, sweet buckwheat noodles, and udon noodles.
Now many of these restaurants have disappeared, and the ones that remain are old restaurants and gourmet restaurants, even receiving Michelin recognition.

Hyundai Department Store's has been in charge of this function for more than 20 years.
Perhaps the only restaurants that have not been replaced at the Hyundai Department Store Trading Branch are the one on the 11th floor and Hansol Naengmyeon in the basement food hall.
That's how Song has already established itself as a popular restaurant for people in the area.
Although it is a simple and classic snack, it has both a luxurious and casual feel, so it is liked by both men and women of all ages, and even children who used to eat with their parents naturally come back to it when they leave home, creating a virtuous cycle routine.

The dumplings are delicious. It's good because the chives are chewy and the seasoning doesn't taste too much.
It's better to eat it while it's hot, so I recommend eating it right away when it's served.
Maybe it feels like a luxurious version of the whole dumplings from the snack shop in front of Beojeong back in the day.

To be honest, the sweet tsuyu and chewy buckwheat noodles are a taste that depends on your taste, but if you eat them while reminiscing about the old taste, they also come across as delicious.
For me, my tastes in reality clash with my memories of old tastes, but since memories are more dominant, Song's buckwheat also tastes delicious.

The pork cutlet was also surprisingly good.
The overflowing cheese and crispy fried meat are as good as any other pork cutlet restaurant.
No, it's better!

Actually, my favorite menu item is stone pot udon.
It's a smooth and light udon, but if you eat it hot with pickled radish in it, it's surprisingly delicious.

The food overall is bland and not seasoned well.
Perhaps because it tastes like this, it may not be a burden to feed it to young children.
The snack shop called Song is bound to become imprinted on the brains of children who are accustomed to this taste.
Noodles and dumplings eaten at the department store haha

Houses like this are rare in Gangnam.
So its value feels more precious.
Please stay with us for a long time haha

PS: My parents have been eating here at our house, and my kids love it too. For our family, it has become a home for three generations.

#Samseong-dong #Hatcho

"Okonomiyaki that does a good job"

There used to be a place in COEX Mall that sold southern American food that tasted like junk food.
Business seemed to be going well, but one day it closed and new construction began.
A new okonomiyaki restaurant is opening.

As time passed by and I passed by here, an okonomiyaki restaurant was established and doing business.
There aren't that many customers because the open-cut food hasn't been eaten yet.
Customers also hesitate after looking at the menu and sometimes turn away.
Still, I wanted to experience it once, so I sat down at a table in front of a large iron plate and placed my order.

The main menu is Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki and sauce yakisoba.
There are also gyoza and egg rolls, so it's not bad to have a light drink.

I ordered from the set menu.
Add squid to.
Shoyuyakisoba
gyoza
It is structured like this.

** Please note that there is no price advantage even if you order it as a set. The price ordered individually and the set price are the same.

#okonomiyaki
It's better than I thought.
When I added squid, it had quite a squid feel.
There are a lot of waves, so it has a Japanese feel.
The taste is a little different than the local taste.
Still, it's nice to have a beer and enjoy the atmosphere.
Instead, since seaweed and katsuobushi are taking a backseat because of negi, next time I will try the traditional okonomi menu.

#yakisoba
Yakisoba is more delicious.
You don't have to use egg yolk, but egg fans will like it even more.
Super ginger adds an accent to the basic taste of Yakisoba.

#gyoja
The gyoza is better than expected.
My expectations were quite low as they were baking something like frozen bibigo royal gyoza, but I guess it was probably an OEM product given the recipe by a franchise.
The seasoning is not strong and there is almost no seasoning taste. The juiciness of the meat is also satisfying.
An unexpected gyoza restaurant.

#Conditions
Condiments such as additional sauces, mayonnaise, and chili peppers are well prepared, and additional side dishes such as vinegared ginger are also provided when you tell them.

#Disappointing point
The disappointing thing is that although the clerks are very friendly, they have no knowledge about food.
The conditions seem to be quite varied, but seaweed powder, the lifeblood of okonomiyaki, is missing.
There was no sancho powder, which would have been better if it had been present.
It's just my own greed, but if you were to open a fancy restaurant at this price, I hope you would pay attention to these details.

PS: There were two types of chefs in front of Tepan.
1. The person who cooks silently - the person who makes okonomiyaki. thanks.
2. Two people chatting and cooking without wearing masks - they seem to be very comfortable working.

reviews.author: ch. “Connoisseur” Paik
reviews.text:
Hana Sha Negative (4.7/5.0)
Pork shabu-shabu set ₩21,000 / Mushroom assorted basket ₩3,000 / Junmai laurel wreath ₩28,000 / Otoko 300 ₩13,000 / Senpuku Junmai 300 ₩15,000

This is an authentic shabu-shabu restaurant that opened in 1993 in the middle of Samseong-dong and has been in operation for over 30 years.
The goal is different from the Suki-style or domestically produced shabu-shabu, which is served with chili sauce or finished with kalguksu and porridge, such as Jeongseongbon and Chaeseondang, which have been mushrooming since the late 1990s.
The daughter, who inherited the spirit of the first lady boss, presents authentic ‘shabu-shabu’ (standard dictionary) with consistent taste.
The figures filled among the monotone stone floor, Japanese house-style walls, and walnut furniture are cute and comfortable.
The first table at every table is sold out, with reservations required, and after that, walk-in guests dine without reservations.
The menu, which was chic and 'fashionable' before the move, has now become more 'customer-friendly' by using large, colorful fonts to improve readability. Maybe it's because the captain changed.
Except for the menu, everything remains the same, especially the original taste.
All guests get to choose between 'beef' shabu and 'pork' shabu, and most (wisely) choose pork. Oh, and of course the cows are great too.
The clear broth begins to heat in one pot per person at the counter and one pot per two people at the table.
Cabbage salad, sesame sauce, ponzu sauce, and pickled onions are served next to the hollow plate.
There are two choices for sauce, sesame and ponzu, but pickled onions also qualify as a third choice.
One vegetable basket per person consisting of bok choy, vitamins, and chives. It's not unlimited refills, but the server is generous enough to catch the remaining meat in advance and ask if you want to refill. The intensity of the fire and the amount of broth are also regularly managed.
Now, a plate full of very thinly rolled pink pork shoulder was served. It feels like eating 130 grams thinly and widely.
The mushroom assorted basket is generously filled with konjac, tofu, enoki mushrooms, and king oyster mushrooms.
I took a bite of the clean broth that said no seasoning was added, but it was quite bland.
According to the guide, you should add all the white vegetables, mushrooms, and konjac first, then scoop them out onto each plate, and blanch the green vegetables for less than 1 minute to prevent them from becoming tough. Paper-like pork is easy to eat in about 15 seconds.
Pork fat fills the light broth with a rich flavor. The dried meat is very soft and easy to swallow with minimal mastication.
It is a richness that is on a different level from the savory flavor of cows. Wrap the meat with cabbage and bok choy and enjoy the harmony of meat and vegetable juice filling your mouth.
The fragrant ponzu sauce and sweet pickled onions work together fantastically, but the taste is best after dipping half of it in the savory and moist sesame sauce.
Although I miss the scent of crown daisy, which was the star of yesteryear, bok choy and chives, the leaders of today's vegetable section, are trustworthy allies that support the flavor of the meat without overshadowing it.
The longer the vegetables and meat are steeped, the thicker the broth and the better it tastes.
Because it has a clean taste, I think it goes really well with soft sake rather than strong shochu.
The 300ml small sake would be a welcome choice for solo guests or those with drinks.
After the addition of meat, the highlight of this meal, the udon making, begins.
Thanks to the thicker broth, the darker the grease marks on the top of the pot, the more delicious the udon will be.
The owner adds white noodles, fried tofu, and oden, and adds the homemade udon sauce twice to adjust the seasoning.
Once it boils, put it on a plate and add about half a teaspoon of shichimi. The chewy noodles and slightly spicy soup are the highlight.
This is why many people remember this play as their last udon. I suddenly remember the single pot udon menu that was sold for 6,000 won.
After drinking the last of the soup and resting for a bit, plum tea is served to refresh your mouth.
Hana Shabu-jeong is the best Japanese shabu-sabu restaurant, a little different from omotenashi, with a unique friendly atmosphere.

reviews.author: Zhseki
reviews.text:
I went to Noya located at COEX.
Noya is a shabu-shabu restaurant with a clean interior.
I visited for dinner on the last day of the holiday and got in right away without waiting. You can order using the tablet at the table.  I ordered the unlimited wagyu and pork belly course. Various mushrooms and vegetables, fish balls, bunmoja, wagyu beef, pork belly, and basic side dishes are provided. The basic side dishes are kimchi crust and gungchae. The mushrooms and vegetables provided were very fresh, and the quality of the meat was excellent. If you order additional meat or vegetables, a robot will bring them to you. Lastly, I ordered porridge and ate it. Parking is provided for 50,000 won or more for 1 hour.
It's been a while since I had shabu-shabu at a clean and delicious restaurant. I enjoyed it so much.

reviews.text:

29000? Shrimp wrapped in lobster and gamtae

reviews.author: Supri
reviews.text: I visited an izakaya with a nice atmosphere near COEX Mall in Gangnam. The atmosphere was very nice and cozy, and most of all, I liked that the tables were private. The weather was cool, so we were able to have a great time feeling the breeze at the terrace-like table. We ordered sashimi, charcoal grilled skewer set, and oden soup for two. Everything was delicious and I ate it with a highball and it went well together. All of the sashimi was fresh and of good quality. And the soup, which is a must-eat when going to an izakaya, was perfect for this weather. All the staff were friendly and I was able to spend the evening pleasantly. I want to visit again next time and try other menu items :) If you are looking for an izakaya near Samseong Station, I recommend this place~

reviews.text:
I was in a slump in my cooking life.
Then I discovered a place called Jeongwoo in Samseong-dong.

reviews.author: K
reviews.text: Sponsored // Dining at Kushiil Oi was a truly satisfying experience. In particular, the skewers grilled on binchotan charcoal had a subtle charcoal-like aroma, and I was impressed by the flavor that spread out the moment you put it in your mouth, and you could also feel the freshness of the ingredients themselves. I ordered Kush Set A, and it had a variety of ingredients, including pork belly, pork belly, and tomato, so it was fun to eat each one. In particular, the tomato and bacon skewers had a unique taste with the juiciness and acidity combined. The seasonal uni and sweet shrimp sashimi were also very fresh, and I really liked the sweetness that lingered in my mouth when I ate the sweet shrimp with seaweed, salt, and wasabi. I drank two types of highballs, and the Jinpa Sikwasa Highball was refreshing and clean, so it went well with the food. The atmosphere of the store was quiet and cozy, making it easy to have a conversation, and the staff were kind enough to help explain the menu, so even if it was your first time there, there was no inconvenience. If you are looking for a quiet and high-quality izakaya near Samseong Station, I recommend you visit.

reviews.text: I visited Ranjuku because a customer came from far away. reviews.text:
Good value Japanese restaurant near Seonjeongneung Royal Tombs…

- Sashimi: tuna, flounder, salmon, sea bream, scallop, etc.
- Sushi: Tuna, eel sushi (2 pieces per person)

- Fried squid
- Steamed cypress wood: brisket (?), mushrooms, pumpkin, bean sprouts, etc.
- Meal: Somen

It feels closer to a Japanese course or set than an omakase, but unless you're visiting with gourmets, you can have a cheap(?) meal in Gangnam with a decent atmosphere.

The sushi was a bit disappointing, but the sashimi was ok, and I personally highly recommend the grilled eel sushi & seaweed / steamed cypress tree / mochiri dofu!!

Izakaya located on the first basement level of Golden Tower near POSCO intersection.

A variety of private rooms are available to suit the number of people. For lunch, we offer a two-course meal and a la carte menu, and for dinner, we offer a full-course meal with an additional menu and several a la carte dishes.

reviews.text:
[Black Truffle Peking Duck]
. Gold dust and truffles are added to regular Beijing khaoya, making it look very gorgeous. The truffle flavor is not overpowering and goes well with the sauce, green onions, and cucumber. However, I personally prefer the simpler, basic Peking duck.

[Main Menu]

. ​Kkanpunggi: Suitable as a side dish for drinks thanks to the spicy sauce.
. ​Meals: The basic menu items, fried rice and jjamppong, are delicious and plentiful. It is recommended to order it together with Mara Hwanggwa to cut down on the greasiness.
. ​Black Garlic Sweet and Sour Pork: It's just regular sweet and sour pork with a few pieces of black garlic, so it's somewhat passable.
[​Services and Accessibility]
. The service is good overall. It is very close to COEX and has good accessibility.

reviews.author: YennaPPa (Luscious.K)
reviews.text:
#Samseong-dong #Wheat field

“A great radish kimchi restaurant”

It is a fairly famous kalguksu restaurant in COEX, Samseong-dong, and its radish noodles, perilla sesame kalguksu, and kalguksu are quite famous.
There is always a wait at lunchtime, so I visited for lunch on a day when I was craving kalguksu.

#kimchi
There is a menu based on young radish, so they serve young radish kimchi and cabbage pancake.
Yeolradish kimchi is quite delicious. Cabbage geotjeori is plain.

#bibimbap
Restaurants of this type usually serve barley rice, but here they serve a small amount of black rice per bowl.
It's a pity, but it's worth eating.

#kalguksu
It's not the taste of a restaurant, but it's surprising that it's not much different from the taste of large companies selling it on the market.
The texture of kalguksu is just like noodles, with no special features such as chewy or soft.
It's quite disappointing for me.

#Perilla Seed Sujebi
The perilla seed soup is bland and soft, which reduces its appeal, and the texture of the sujebi is also dry.
It's also disappointing.

It's fall, but considering the temperature is above 25 degrees and we are in a restaurant where we eat hot food, shouldn't we be air-conditioning?
I remember coming out sweating profusely because it was really hot.

reviews.author: Yijin Kim (Jane)
reviews.text:
Perilla seed sujebi and stir-fried octopus!
I was a little disappointed that there was no boiled pork, so I ordered stir-fried octopus!

Perilla Seed Sujebi / It’s so light, savory, not greasy, and chewy. It's not too thick, but it's not too watery either, so it's very delicious. The thickness of the sujebi is just right!

Stir-fried octopus/ Octopus is cooked quickly over high heat until it becomes soft and soft. Not tough! There wasn't a lot of water, and because they didn't use red pepper paste, the taste was spicy and refreshing without any harshness. It was really amazing how somen didn't swell like this.
The seasoning for stir-fried octopus was refreshing, so I mixed it with somen and topped it with young radish kimchi. So, Yeolradish Kimchi Bibim Noodles was born! It was a very hearty and filling meal.

reviews.author: Matboard Chart
reviews.text:
A high-end, authentic Sichuan cuisine restaurant where you will be overwhelmed once by the atmosphere and twice by the taste.
It's great from the exterior to the interior. The interior is clean and sophisticated enough to make you think it's a Chinese restaurant, and the red peppers at the store's entrance are impressive.
The interior has a nice interior filled with glasses and alcohol on one wall, and even the table and lighting have a subtle, luxurious feel.

I ate a course meal. Basically, everything is delicious and has a slightly spicy base.
Although it was spicy, I was able to enjoy it comfortably. It's been a while since I had a very delicious Chinese meal. In particular, I felt like I had to come back and eat the jjamppong and fried rice again.

Palbochae
It had a bit of a fire flavor, and the seafood was fresh. In particular, the squid was very chewy!

Nanjawans
The outside was crispy and the inside was softer.

Rajji
To put it simply, it is boneless chicken. It's not just spicy, it's the kind of spicy that makes your mouth feel a little tingly.

Mango Shrimp
The meat was plump and the sauce was very sweet and delicious. 2 per person.

3-piece meal menu set
Jajangmyeon – It’s okay~
Jjambbong - What is the soup? Delicious... Tdabon
Fried rice - Wow! Merge? The taste of fire is very strong! Taddabon

It's been a while since I had a very satisfying Chinese course meal. There was always something disappointing, but it wasn't here~

reviews.author: Kyeongbae Hwang
reviews.text: It is a collection of Sichuan cuisine and representative Chinese dishes that are slightly Koreanized and less burdensome to eat.  I definitely recommend starting with the Shih Tzu cold assorted vegetables as an appetizer. Sea and land dishes are perfect as appetizers.  Rajji, it's good because it's Sichuan style - some people may not be familiar with it.  Sweet and sour pork is completely Korean. Yangju fried rice is good because the rice grains are still alive, and the Fujian-style weak oyster sauce(?) is mixed with rich seafood.  Both passed!  I need to try more different dishes next time. The service is good, but the sound inside seems a bit noisy.

reviews.author: Eat it all Ryan eatitall
reviews.text:
Samseong Station Hotel Chinese Restaurant Ewhawon is located on the 3rd floor of Hotel Oakwood Premier, so it is a Chinese restaurant with friendly staff, good accessibility among 5-star Chinese restaurants, and good value for money in terms of menu and price.

​We hold a lot of year-end gatherings, and we have a variety of rooms to suit the needs of those looking for a gathering place in Samseong-dong, and the luxurious interior enhances the quality of the gathering.

​Baekhwago Chicken Soup, a health food, has a taste that breaks your preconceptions about health food.

I was surprised that the soft and chewy Baekhwago and Chicken Soup had a clean, non-greasy broth.

​Zwixia, which means drunken king prawn, is delicious dipped in sauce with Sohongju added or slightly dipped in soy sauce. The plump shrimp meat and aroma are addictive.

​The beef jangmyeon, seafood jjamppong, and japchae rice that I ordered for the meal menu were also of a high standard, so I was able to continue the happy feeling I had after eating the main menu.

​The last dessert, mango sago, was sweet and sour, so it was the perfect ending.
​
One of the advantages of the hotel's Chinese restaurant is the support for parking. You can also shop at COEX with 3 hours of free parking when dining, so keep this in mind!

reviews.text:
Order menu: Half chadol jjamppong, half truffle jjajang, mapo tofu + fried rice, caviar menbosha

reviews.text:
I went to Haidilao COEX branch.
I have been to Haidilao many times in China, but this is my first time in Korea. I visited around 3pm on a Monday and there was no wait. Although there were several groups of guests, there were many empty seats and it was more relaxed than expected.
To the lunch menu for 3 people, I added an extra soup and ordered additional items that were not included in the lunch set.
I chose tomato, mushroom, and cheongyumara soup and added pepper soup. From the lunch set selection menu, I chose the recommended hot pot menu, mushrooms, tofu, glass noodles, 2 vegetables, and 3 beef sirloin.
Additionally, I ordered shrimp balls, fried soybean skin, kung fu noodles, assorted cheonyeop, special beef, cotton tofu, and soft tofu.
We made several sauces to suit our taste at the sauce bar. The sauce bar not only had sauces, but also shrimp porridge, nabak kimchi, and cabbage kimchi, as well as konjac noodles, seasoned fish skin, and fruit for dessert.
The staff brought soup, but only plain water was served without the added pepper soup. I spoke to the staff and they brought the sauce and diluted it with water at the table.
Even though I make sauce at the sauce bar, eat shrimp porridge, and eat food, the soup does not boil. I spoke to the staff and only then did they turn on the induction. They told me to add vegetables, so I added them, but they didn't even boil.
Haidilao, a hotpot chain famous for its service in China, is strange. I had many good memories in Haidilao, China, but I am a little disappointed.
The cotton tofu and soft tofu had a good texture. The kung fu noodles were made directly at the table by the staff, and it had the feel of dosak noodles and was delicious. Thousand leaves are much tougher than those found in China. The special beef has a strange texture and taste. It is unique to eat seasoned beef in soup.
There are some regrets, perhaps because I had high expectations when I visited, but it's been a while since I had delicious hot pot.

A Chinese restaurant located in the food alley across from the City Airport Tower in Samseong-dong, Gangnam-gu.

This place, which opened not very long ago, is run by Chinese people and serves beef noodles as its main dish, as well as a variety of local Chinese dishes.

The characteristic feature of the beef noodle soup here is that the menu is divided according to the type of noodle and the soup base. All noodles are homemade, the broth is made from homemade broth, and the garnish of generously boiled meat is especially tender and delicious.
In addition, the portions are so generous that it is not enough for a meal, so many people visit during lunch time to the extent that there is a waiting line.

However, the beef noodles are good, but what is disappointing is the dim sum and the price...

I tried two types of dim sum, but both were very poor compared to the price. In particular, the xiao long bao was not very juicy and the taste was very different from what I expected, so I personally do not recommend it.

This is Gangnam Yeonga, a newly opened Chinese restaurant in Samseong-dong.
I made a reservation for Saturday lunch through Naver Reservation and visited.
I ordered lazuji, red beef, gongsimchae, and a lunch set. For the lunch set, I ordered a 2-person set consisting of Chungkyeong somen, chive clam rice bowl, and stir-fried crab, and a 2-person set consisting of XO fried rice, chive clam rice bowl, and stir-fried crab.
As is typical of Sichuan cuisine, the razuji is stir-fried with sancho and dried peppers to give it a Szechuan feel, and the red beef tastes like a cross between red beef and dongpo meat. The meat size is red beef, the sauce is dongpo meat, and the meat texture is medium. I wish the Gongsimchae had been stir-fried a little less to give it a crunchy texture. The chive clam rice bowl was spicy and delicious, and the XO fried rice was also delicious. Stir-fried crab seemed to be fried and seasoned, but it was good because it had a lot of meat and the crab shell was thin.
I had a delicious lunch with my family.

reviews.author: YennaPPa (Luscious.K)
reviews.text:
“As expected, I love Weiru.”

I heard that the menu changed after the summer, so I visited again this winter.
The reason why I often visit Weiru is because of the simple food, the taste that is faithful to the ingredients, the taste of the food that lives up to its name, and most of all, the excellent black bean noodles.

#Peking duck
It was still delicious, but the duck that day was a little overcooked.
If you ask for a lot of meat, it's good to carve it with a lot of meat potion, and if you ask for a leg, they serve it generously.
If you have children who like meat, you can ask them like this.

Since it is a square pancake, it is easy to wrap and eat.
Conditions that are not visible elsewhere are good.
In particular, sugar and minced garlic are the cheat keys to making Peking duck much more delicious!

#Snow crab meat soup
The large amount of snow crab meat and mild flavor are excellent.
The temperature is scorching because it was not just served, but rather steamed.
The temperature enhances the taste even more.
It would be even better if only the swim bladder was included here haha.

#dim sum
The three types of dim sum are somehow different from typical high-end Chinese food.
It doesn't taste like seasoning, so it's simple and the full texture is transmitted through your teeth.
Dim sum pi is also satisfactory.

#Gungbo Lobster
It's not Kung Pao Chicken, it's Kung Pao Lobster.
Is Kung Pao a top-class dish? Hahaha
Surprisingly, lobster has a springy texture that matches the intensity of the Kung Pao sauce.

#Songi beef
The chewy texture of the beef, which was a bit disappointing last time, has now become perfectly soft.
A large amount of natural bunches symbolize the hotel Chinese food.

#sweet and sour pork
Sweet and sour pork is really good.
The deep-fried meat is crispy and the sweet and sour pork sauce has a good balance of sweet, salty, and sour flavors.
Sweet and sour pork with an elegant taste that is quite different from those that are only sweet or spicy.
It fits my mouth perfectly.

#Jjajangmyeon
Until now, it had been a very freshly stir-fried Jjajang-like Jajangmyeon, but this time it was a little closer to Jjajang.
The taste is still deep and wide. Instead, the onions are a little saltier and softer than before.
It's really delicious even if you add a lot of cilantro. #Goshjjajangmyeon haha

#dessert
I thought they would give me a shimmy, but I got a fine dining-style dessert.
Chinese cookie-like texture and soft jam? And dried pineapple haha
It's an unexpected dessert, but it goes well after a meal.

The upgrade of the dessert commensurate with the price is impressive.

#service
Among the services of a 5-star hotel, it is good to recognize the service of Parnas.
I was treated very warmly, and the night view from the 34th floor was a bonus.

reviews.author: Seunggu Choe
reviews.text:
I went to COEX to run an errand and stopped by ‘Misari Milbit Chogye Noodles Samsung COEX Mall Branch’ just in time for lunch. Restaurants in COEX are always crowded, but the store here is very spacious, so I was able to eat relatively leisurely even during busy times.

The advantage of this place is that it offers a wide range of dishes, from summer menus such as cool Chogye noodles and Chogye bibim noodles, to warm noodles such as Ongyejin kalguksu, mushroom chicken gaejang, and perilla chicken kalguksu, and soup menus such as Chogye chicken gomtang and Byeongcheon sundae soup. I thought it was a good place to grab a quick meal.

I ordered the signature dish, chogye noodles. I was able to enjoy it refreshingly in the hot early summer weather, but it didn't taste as special as the chogye noodles I've had elsewhere before. The king dumplings I ordered as a side also tasted ordinary and average rather than very special.

The group I visited with chose the warm soup menu, and overall, they didn't seem to be very satisfied.

In general, the 'Misari Milbit Chogye Noodles' Samsung COEX Mall branch is a good option when you want a quick and easy meal in COEX. Thanks to the diverse menu and spacious store, it was nice to eat comfortably in the crowded COEX.

#Samseong-dong #Dowon Style

“Change that has been devastating”

Dowon Style, a subgroup of Plaza Hotel’s Dowon.
Even though it is a sub-brand, the price is not that cheap and is in the mid-range price range.
Was it last year... I reevaluated the Dowon style after eating it as a lunch course, the fruit sweet and sour pork that inherited Dowon's authenticity, the well-made black bean noodles, and the dishes and temperature that were better than expected.

With those expectations, I also visited the Plaza Hotel Dowon, the origin of this restaurant, which I recently visited, and was satisfied with it, but I feel very sad because it completely fell short of my expectations.

The existing fruit sweet and sour pork menu has disappeared, and the Tomahawk sweet and sour pork, which only looks good but has no difference in taste, is quite disappointing.

The price has risen a lot.
It may seem like a trick to raise prices.

It could also be seen as a trick to raise the bar.

The taste was poor
the price went up

It's disappointing.

reviews.author: WOONG’s KITCHEN
reviews.text:
Baek Ga-hyang. There aren't really many places to eat around Samseong Station. On this day, after finishing a small but not easy report, I was wandering around trying to figure out where to go after work to unwind and think about what to do next. I found a new Chinese restaurant and decided to visit it.

Following the opinions of my colleagues, I ordered nanjawansu and sweet and sour pork and decided to try the meal menu. The Nanjawans that came out first were delicious compared to the ones I had waited for without thinking. It was well cooked on the outside and inside, and the fried portion on the outside absorbed a lot of the sauce and was seasoned well. Served with properly cooked vegetables is the icing on the cake. The sweet and sour pork with a fluffy texture is initially served as a side dish, so it would be a good idea to inform those who want to eat it in advance.

It turned out that Hosingak, a well-established restaurant across the street from Samseong-dong, had opened a new store. One of the employees I went with was a lunch regular at Hosingak, so I exchanged greetings with the owner and got Jjambbong soup as a free meal. Accordingly, I ordered red pepper tray jjajang and fried rice.

The meal menu was good, the spicy stir-fried jjajang with various ingredients was good, and the fried rice with each grain coated was also good.

I'll have to stop by during lunch time sometime soon. It’s very nice because it’s located nearby🤩

#Samseong-dong #Bongeunsa Temple #Seoraewon

“Price is the problem”

Bongeunsa Temple's restaurant is Seoraewon, and usually religious facilities provide offerings (Bulgoese style) or love feasts (Christian style) for free.
But this place, like a restaurant, sells for money.
It is the largest temple in Seoul and has many believers, so it would be difficult to provide it for free.
So, I visited a restaurant that I had been curious about for a long time.

The day of my visit was the day before Buddha's Birthday, so there were a lot of believers and tourists, and the weather was nice so it was nice to take a walk around the temple.
The noodles you eat afterwards cannot be tasteless.

Still, if we talk about the exact taste, the taste of the noodles themselves is not that good.
Since ingredients such as anchovies cannot be used, the depth of the soup is significantly shallow.
Instead, it has a mild umami flavor but is not attractive.
Bibim noodles are sweeter than sour, so it feels like a light bowl rather than a very tasty dish.
Instead, the quantity is not bad.

The price of banquet noodles and bibim noodles are both 6,000 won... which is a disappointing price compared to the taste.
Considering it is a religious facility, the price is disappointing.
I don't know if it is operated directly by Bongeunsa Temple or if it is outsourced, but it is not a noodle worth paying to eat despite this level of hassle and inconvenience.
I miss the noodles I eat at home even more.

PS: The fight to find a spot is a competition for survival.

PS2: Is 12,000 won for soft tofu jjamppong a scam?
Is it reasonable to call it #gongyanggan at this price?

“A place famous for simple Andong Guksi”

The back alleys of Samseong-dong are no different from the foodie areas of the back alleys of the city’s company town.
Since there are so many restaurants and bars, there are many different types of products, and it is famous for Andong Guksi, so it is so popular that there is no time to stop by during lunch time.

The characteristic of Soyeon is that the soup is clear like Gomguksi, rather than the white soup like the familiar Andong Guksi, and as a result, the richness of the soup is light and refreshing.
Although the soup has a little help from Masitgun, it is good because it is rich and refreshing.
The noodles are extremely soft, but the flavor of the soup soaks in well and goes down without any hassle.
Instead, as I continued to eat it, it felt a little greasy, so I added unlimited side dishes such as steamed perilla leaves and pickled vegetables.

The side dish is steamed perilla leaf soy sauce, the symbol of Andong Guksijip.
It is very delicious with just the right amount of saltiness and softness. I liked it so much that I ordered it twice more.

Potato pancakes are truly unique.
I fried the finely ground potatoes as is, frying only one side and keeping the other side soft.
It's as if only one side of the tuna's belly meat was flattened to give it the taste of raw tuna and a fiery taste at the same time.
It's crispy and light, but it's a bit overcooked so it tastes burnt.

Nevertheless, it is a fairly simple and delicious Andong guksi restaurant.
Perhaps because I visited when I was sick, I feel like the hot soup helped me recover.

I guess it’s the same #food origin!

reviews.author: YennaPPa (Luscious.K)
reviews.text:
#Samseong-dong #Cheon Mi-hyang

“I passed the test at a local Chinese restaurant.”

1. No one can deny that this is a place that left a mark on Gangnam Chinese restaurants. Ilhyang expanded its branches, but as a result, there were many chefs who worked at Ilhyang, and as they spread, something called Ilhyang was created. Ilhyang style can be immediately sensed in the sweet and sour pork and jjambbong.

2. The most famous branch from Ilhyang is Chef Song. Chef Song is the standard of Cheongchuleoram and has already broken away from Ilhyang's shadow and shows the level of Ilhyang's superiors. Another pruning restaurant is Cheonmimi. This place started as a 24-hour high-end Chinese restaurant in Garosu-gil, but although it has not developed to the level of Chef Song, it seems to be continuing its legacy to some extent.

3. The Chinese restaurant I’m curious about is Cheonmihyang. It's a place with quite a few branches, and the food is top-notch, but the prices are a bit more expensive than local Chinese restaurants. As the name suggests, maybe a cheaper version of Cheonmimi? It might be. (If anyone knows the facts, please let me know in the comments.)

4. While searching for a local Chinese restaurant, I found that there was Cheonmihyang in my neighborhood, so I went there and was more satisfied than I expected.
Basically, sweet and sour pork is a daily style of thick meat and fluffy batter, and it is seasoned to some extent, so it is delicious even without sauce.
The sauce is sweet, sour, and soy sauce-flavored, and the meat is thick, so it goes well with the sauce.
This is a very satisfying sweet and sour pork.

5. The Jjajangmyeon is better than any other Jjajangmyeon restaurant in this neighborhood.
It's similar to semi-uni jjajang with a little minced meat, and the chunjang (chunjang) is quite bitter and the sweetness isn't too much, so I'm quite satisfied.
Perhaps the best quality of Jjajangmyeon in this neighborhood.

6. Jjambbong is Cheonmihyang’s signature.
I asked for the three-lined dish, so there were plenty of ingredients and it felt rich overall.
The moment I tasted the soup, it felt exactly like jjamppong, so I thought my imagination number 3 might be true.
It's a jjamppong that emulsifies well and retains a nutty flavor. It's not spicy, but light, and I was satisfied with the slightly spicy scent.
However, although it may be due to the price, the overall freshness of the seafood feels low, which is an improvement for this restaurant.

7. For a local Chinese restaurant, this is acceptable. It's a good place to come and eat out with your family.
If you have trouble choosing, it's a good geographical location to go to Inamjang on the 1st floor.

PS: Japchaebap wasn't bad either.

“A store with a kind-hearted owner who does a lot of community service.”

A local Chinese restaurant in Samseong-dong.

You can also become a volunteer firefighter haha.

The owner is also kind-hearted and generous enough to provide free popsicles in the past and free slush desserts these days.

The owner’s specialty is growing fish and coral reefs.
There are two very beautiful coral reef tanks and tropical fish for the coral.
Five or six water tanks are managed with each theme.
At this level, there is no need to go to the aquarium, and it is fun to see wonderful fish tanks.

In terms of taste alone, it's disappointing to me.
In particular, the lack of seasoning is not suitable for Chinese food and the taste is worse when delivered, but many people like this restaurant's food because it has a healthy taste.

reviews.author: ANNEZUE
reviews.text:
I ordered a set menu for 2 people.
Mango Lassi was delicious. It was a proper yogurt drink with ripe mango floating in it. It was delicious.
The milk tea was a delicious drink with a strong black tea flavor. It's better to go to a clumsy cafe and drink milk tea here.
The staff was friendly, but it was disappointing that there were no sanitary gloves in the store. My hands were sticky with seasoning, so I wanted to eat cleanly, but the female staff member informed me that there were no sanitary gloves in the store. I ordered two of the representative menu items, butter chicken makhni and chicken vindaloo curry, but the taste was just a vague Korean-style curry with a lot of tomato flavor. If you look at the taste of the curry, it's not good. Looking at the overall thing, it's okay. The lassi was delicious and the mango salad was delicious, but the salad had mango. What was included was also unique, and I wrapped it in naan and dipped it in the sauce. The combination of food was really good. The taste of the sauce was good, and the combination of the mango, salad, and naan was good, so I ate it with satisfaction. The tandoori chicken was edible. It was just ordinary chicken that was roughly cooked, but the sauce was sweet and sour, so I enjoyed it.
There are a lot of places to eat nearby, so I don't think I'll ever have to come here again. I ate my fill.

reviews.author: Youngmin SUH
reviews.text:
This is a franchise restaurant famous for Vietnamese pho, and you can eat Vietnamese pho along with Pomaine and Le Saigon in COEX.
Unlike in the past, as more and more Vietnamese pho restaurants have opened, it is true that people are less satisfied with the taste of franchise stores like Pho Bay, but it is also a place where you can conveniently eat pho when you want to eat it near where you work or visit.
In the case of the COEX branch, the food comes out quickly in a large space, which is an advantage, and it is a place where you can eat without any worries even if it is a little after meal time.
There may be some complaints about the price or taste, but since there are not many other alternatives in COEX, it can be seen as a relatively thankful place in that respect.

reviews.author: BONG BONG
reviews.text:
Worst service experienced by fellow Koreans
Even when we tried to place an order and raised our hand to call out, the clerk didn't come and even though we took our menu orders, people who came in later than us got their menus first.
I didn't say that the menu I ordered was one that took a long time or that if it took a long time because there were a lot of customers, it would come out late due to a backlog of orders. However, the menu wasn't something that required a lot of work like fried food or spring rolls. If I ordered rice noodles, they didn't even provide bean sprouts or pickled radish by default, so I asked the part-time workers and the person who looked like the boss to go to the kitchen directly, but they refused to listen. Fortunately, one of the part-time workers was kind.
Honestly, I would like to make a suggestion to the head office. I have never been to a restaurant like this before, but this one is the worst.

reviews.author: DASIT
reviews.text:
A Thai cuisine restaurant located in the Samseong-dong food alley across from the city airport terminal...

This is a place where you can experience the cooking of local Thai chefs, and you can taste a variety of representative Thai dishes.

The characteristic of this place is that it feels closer to the taste of hotel-style food for foreigners rather than the taste experienced locally. As a result, the scent is not strong and the taste seems to be a bit strong. Still, it's enough to enjoy the unique Thai cuisine, and the price isn't too expensive, so you don't have to worry about it.

The unfortunate thing is that I want to keep the tom yum goong warm and eat it, but that doesn't work...
I think it would be a good idea to add a little solid fuel to the bottom of the pot to keep it hot.

On the first floor, you can look at the menu and order directly, and on the second floor, you can order through a kiosk, and the locals who serve you are very friendly.
